chapter: Chicago years: recordings, Armstrong, wartime exit
title: Playing blues at the Firehouse on Clark Street for white jazz fans
summary: On Clark Street he played the blues all night for white fans who came to hear New Orleans blues, some of whom sat in. He does not recall their names, and notes record collectors.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I see. Well, Herb, what else were you doing about 1937 or 38? Can you tell us something of your experience?

Well, I was in Chicago, playing with different bunches, you know what I mean? I played on Clark Street at the Firehouse. Many jazz fans used to come there and have me to play the blues all night. They'd come in, I mean white jazz fans, they'd come in and treat me well, just to hear the blues. Of course, around Chicago they didn't care much about the New Orleans blues. But they used to come in there and they really used to enjoy the blues. That's all they'd ask me to play. They liked blues in Chicago. The old Bauhaus, New Orleans blues. That's what they wanted.
In other words, the white people in the locality of Chicago and elsewhere were becoming aware of this music called jazz. Yeah. And they had certain forms that were interesting to them.
Yeah. And they could play it too because they'd come and sit in with us and play, you know what I mean? Quite a few of them.
Who were some of these people who sat in with you, Herb, and with whom you played? Did you ever come to them?

Well, you know, it slips your memory. You know, you soon forget about names and you meet so many musicians. But, you know, just like if you'd be out and you'd know where there's a band playing, you'd go anywhere, you'd be introduced, you'd sit out. And then maybe you wouldn't see them for quite a while after, or the slip of, you know, the remembrance of them.

That was the era of time around when Benny Goodman and Mesereau and Dave Tuff and those musicians were in Chicago. Yeah, at that time, yeah. Did you know Mesereau personally? No, I didn't know him personally, no. As you mentioned, record collectors were becoming in existence at that time.
Oh, yeah. Plenty of them, yeah.
